MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 20, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:01 p.m., on May 20, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 15, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:04 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Leckness

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are
  the City and the City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiators are Dennis
  Wilberg and Keith Rattay.

City Council Minutes  1  May 20, 2013
 City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City received correspondence from the State
Department of Finance late last Friday night and he recommended that the Council add an item
to the Closed Session agenda for the purpose of discussing the matter and possibly giving
authorization to add a complaint to the litigation that staff is preparing to file.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to declare a need to
consider a Closed Session matter (CS2) which arose subsequent to the posting of the Agenda and
to affirm that the matter must be considered before the next meeting with the recommendation
that it be addressed in closed session tonight.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel—Consideration of Commencement of Litigation.
  Subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9 (One Potential Case - Challenge to DOF Claim on
  City Funds)

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:11 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for item CS1, the Council received information and
gave direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

The Council also addressed a late-added agenda item (CS2) regarding potential litigation with
the State of California Department of Finance. The discussion was relative to the State DOF's
May 17 letter denying $115,000 in funding for the 2013-14 ROPS period. City Attorney Curley
announced that the City Council authorized staff to add this matter to the litigation that was
authorized at the last meeting. The vote was 4-1 with Council Member Schlicht in dissent. Mr.
Curley stated that Council Member Schlicht has voiced her opinion that this is redevelopment
money residue and the Housing Authority should pay its own way and not seek redevelopment
funds.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Mission Viejo Resident Irene Dressler for her Participation in the Orange
  County Preliminary Pageant of the Ms. Senior California Pageant and Receive Award
  of Appreciation to the City by State Pageant Director Pamela Wheeler

City Council Minutes  2  May 20, 2013
   Mayor Reardon presented the certificate of commendation to Irene Dressler and received
  an award of appreciation from State pageant Director Pamela Wheeler.

P2. Proclaim June 1 through June 8, 2013 as " Paint Our Town Purple Week" in Support
  of Relay for Life

  Mayor Reardon presented the proclamation to Margot Ferron, Event Chair of Relay for
  Life Mission Viejo.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Karen Siegfried: announced that she is employed by All City Management Services, the
company that provides crossing guard services in Mission Viejo. She stated that it has come to
her attention that the City is considering a 25% cut in pay for crossing guards and she asked that
the Council consider the impact of such a pay cut.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley noted that the City does not set the salaries for the crossing guards and
the City does not intend to cut the number of crossing guards.

Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay confirmed that the City does not control the crossing
guards' pay. Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas announced that staff will be going
out to bid for crossing guard services in the coming months in order to get the most competitive
price.

Susan Sellers, President of the Friends of the Mission Viejo Dog Park: announced a fundraising
event "The Boneyard Bash" to be held on Saturday, July 13, 2013, in the Civic Center Kershaw
Garden from 6:00 to 9:00 p.m. Mrs. Sellers noted that the Friends of the Dog Park seek the
Council's support and she asked that the City help promote the event.

Robert David Breton, M.V.: stated that it is heartening to see high school civics class students in
the audience tonight. He commended the library staff for the tremendous effort that they've made
in implementing their goal to develop true partnerships with the schools. Mr. Breton also
announced that the Friends of the Library have agreed to fund the project of converting and
digitizing over 200 valuable films and news reels for the library archive and he hopes that the
project will be done by the time the City celebrates its anniversary this year.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 4, 5, and 10 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  3  May 20, 2013
 AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

3.  Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - Third Quarter of
  FY 2012-13

  Received and filed.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2013

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for March 2013

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March
  2013

  Received and filed.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly
  Report for March 2013

  Received and filed.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

11. Review and Discussion of the Street Sweeping Contract

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  City Attorney Bill Curley answered questions of the City Council.

City Council Minutes  4  May 20, 2013
   Council Member Leckness stated that the requirement in the RFP for the street sweeping
  vehicles to be 2 years-old or newer is excessive and the Council discussed the matter.

  Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to
  amend the RFP and remove the requirement that the street sweeping vehicles be two years-
  old or newer.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ury
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the Minutes (item 16, page 10) do not reflect Mayor
  Reardon's statement that the City Manager will be receiving a written evaluation.

  City Attorney Bill Curley noted that the paper minutes are short, succinct action
  summaries. The Council can also designate that the Granicus recording is an official set of
  Minutes which captures every spoken word.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
  Minutes for regular City Council meeting of May 6, 2013, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register Dated April 26, 2013 in the Amount of $558,543.73

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a payment made to Digital Map Products and she
  noted that the GIS system has never been updated to remove the fire hazard areas that the
  City Council rejected.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  May 20, 2013
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

5.  Check Register Dated May 3, 2013 in the Amount of $1,313,829.48

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment to Go Live Tech for $8,000 for ERP
  software vendor demos.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas responded that Go Live is the outside
  consultant helping staff go through the RFP process for a new accounting software system
  and this was one of the progress payments.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

10. Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Third Quarter of 2012-13

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about $70,000 of estimated grant revenues that have not
  yet been received and she asked if we know what the hold-up is.

  Director Dyas announced that she would have to look into it and staff will get back to the
  Council with a response.

  Council Member Schlicht asked about the Mission Viejo Foundation Fund which has a
  negative cash balance of $100,000. She stated that it hasn't been carried over in the last few
  quarterly financial reports.

  Director Dyas responded that she will follow-up with an explanation.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to receive
  and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  6  May 20, 2013
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

12. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

13. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

14. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

15. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Council Member Ury presented the report and an outline of the 2013-14 OCTA Budget.

16. SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

Orange County Vector Control Board Report

Council Member Leckness presented a report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay drew the Council's attention to
the listing of special events costs which will be discussed during the budget deliberations in June.

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that he is updating the City's contract templates to try and
better capture RFP protocols, bid protest protocols, etc. He asked the Council Members to let
him know if they would like to have some degree of involvement in the update process.

Mr. Curley also noted that he is continuing to monitor the State's proposed further dilution of the
Brown Act and the Public Records Act (PRA.) He stated that legal obligations under the Brown
Act and the PRA could go away, as could AB1234 ethics training requirements. The Department
of Finance will be presenting the matter to the State Mandates Commission and Mr. Curley
announced that he will provide the City Council with updates as they are available.

City Council Minutes  7  May 20, 2013
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

17. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness highlighted a new business, Club Elevate, on the corner of Santa
Margarita Parkway and Marguerite. He shared the story of the owner's enthusiasm for the
products he sells and he encouraged residents to visit the store. Council Member Leckness also
outlined the recent fire alarm installation program at Casta del Sol. He noted that the residents
loved it and he thanked OCFA and City staff for the time and effort involved in creating such a
beneficial program. Lastly, Council Member Leckness commented on yesterday's international
triathlon at Lake Mission Viejo. He enjoyed seeing the athletes in person and he thanked Mayor
Pro Tem Kelley for helping to bring the event back to Mission Viejo six years ago.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht expressed her sadness for the victims of the Oklahoma tornados. She
thanked the Saddleback Republican Assembly for inviting her to be a guest speaker last week
and she noted that she very much enjoyed it. She also discussed her recent trip to an Angels
baseball game via Metrolink. A round trip ticket is $7.00 and she encouraged residents to take
the train to a game at least once. Council Member Schlicht announced that there will be two tea
party rallies on May 21, 2013, to protest the IRS' abuse of power. Both rallies are at IRS offices
beginning at 11:30 a.m. at 24000 Avila Road in Laguna Niguel and 801 Civic Center Drive in
Santa Ana. She stated that we have to break the public apathy and make government realize that
it works for the people, not against its people. Council Member Schlicht concluded her
comments with a quote from Abraham Lincoln: "If you once forfeit the confidence of your
fellow citizens, you can never regain their respect and esteem. It is true that you may fool all of
the people some of the time; you can even fool some of the people all of the time; but you can't
fool all of the people all of the time."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury had no comments.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked Karen Wylie and staff for the excellent job fair that the City
hosted on May 16. She noted that she stopped by for a visit and was pleased to see how many
potential employers and job-seekers attended. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley congratulated Kathy Moon
on her retirement. Ms. Moon, a beloved teacher, impacted thousands of lives through her work as
an educator for 40 years, the last 25 years at Mission Viejo's De Portola Elementary School.
Mayor Pro Tem Kelley also outlined her attendance at the recent composting workshop which

City Council Minutes  8  May 20, 2013
 was hosted by the City and Waste Management. The program was very informative and
something staff could consider filming for Mission Viejo Television in the future. She also
attended the Mission Viejo triathlon which draws a national and international field of
competitors. She stated that the triathlon is very well done and gets better every year, thanks to
Bill Leach and Bob Cuyler who plan the event. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that residents
can see a Coaches Corner segment on the triathlon airing on MVTV in the coming weeks. Other
events coming soon include the KSBR Birthday Bash on Sunday, May 26 and the City's
Memorial Day ceremony on Monday, May 27 at 8:30 a.m. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley encouraged
residents to attend the uplifting, patriotic event and she noted that it is a good time to stop and
thank those who gave it all for our nation. Lastly, she reminded residents of the blood drive on
Friday, June 7 from 12:00 to 6:00 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at City Hall. Reservations are
encouraged and can be made through Mayor Pro Tem Kelley or on the Red Cross website:
redcrossblood.org using the sponsor code COMV.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon read a story from the Mission Viejo Life blog about the Watson family who
recently relocated to Mission Viejo from Australia. After moving here, their 5 year-old daughter
Emma suffered a ruptured appendix and has been hospitalized for 19 days. Neighbors and
friends have rallied around the Watson family delivering meals and cards and the young girl's
classmates pooled their money to buy Emma a mini iPad (with assistance from the local Elks
club.) Mayor Reardon shared photos of young Emma and read Mrs. Watson's comments: "There
is so much negativity in the news these days that I wanted to show how positive and how great
this community is... you just don't hear about this kind of stuff every day. You only hear about it
in fairytales." Mayor Reardon announced that the City hosted a countywide Joint Information
Center exercise and she commended Paul Catsimanes for spearheading the disaster preparedness
exercise. She also discussed her attendance the Santa Margarita Water District stakeholder
meeting and she noted that she has an outline, taken by her intern, which she will email to her
colleagues and anyone who would like a copy. She also attended two recent events surrounding
the prescription drug abuse epidemic. Mayor Reardon was especially impressed by the 16 and 17
year-old former drug addicts who made a presentation to the group. They recognize that they
have to give back as part of their recovery and she stated that it was unbelievable to hear what
they've been through. Mayor Reardon noted that she, Diana Presta and Crime Prevention
Specialist Tammy Descoteaux will be speaking on the subject of prescription drug abuse with the
Rotary Club tomorrow morning. She also outlined her attendance at the grand opening events for
several new businesses, including Elements Therapeutic Massage, FIT Pilates studio, and Stack's
Pancake House. Lastly, Mayor Reardon reminded residents that staff will present the proposed
budget to the City Council on June 3 with a budget workshop following on June 17, 2013. She
recommended that anyone with questions about the budget and how the city is spending its
money should come to the workshop or email the City Council with comments or concerns.

City Council Minutes  9  May 20, 2013
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:31 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting in memory of Council Member Ury's brother, Michael
Ury, to Monday, June 3, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 3, 2013

City Council Minutes  10  May 20, 2013
